Export a Plot to Graphics Files

Source: R/exportPlot.R
exportPlot.Rd

Draws a plot to one or several graphics files (PNG, TIFF, PDF, SVG) in a single call, controlled by a session-wide switch. It is meant for analysis scripts that produce publication figures: the plot call is written once, piped into exportPlot(), and the files are only (re)written when the switch is on. Running a chunk interactively then shows the plot on screen without overwriting the figures produced by an earlier, final run.

options(pharos.exportPlot = TRUE)   # once, at the top of the script

plotXY(y ~ x, data = d) |>
  exportPlot("fig1", type = c("png", "tif"))

Usage

exportPlot(
  expr,
  file,
  type = "png",
  width = 16/3,
  height = width,
  res = 300,
  create = getOption("pharos.exportPlot", FALSE),
  screen = TRUE
)

Arguments

expr

a call that draws a plot, typically piped in with |>, or a braced block of drawing calls. It is not evaluated before exportPlot() runs, and is evaluated several times (see Details).

file

the path of the output file, without extension; one file per element of type is written, with the extension of that type. A trailing extension .png, .tif, .tiff, .pdf or .svg is removed. Required if create = TRUE.

type

one or several of "png", "tif", "pdf" and "svg". Default is "png". TIFF files are LZW-compressed; SVG needs a working cairo device. capabilities("cairo") is not enough to tell: on macOS it can be TRUE while svg() cannot open a device (XQuartz missing). A device that cannot be opened is an error.

width, height

the size of the plot in inches. The default width of 16/3 inches gives 1600 pixels at 300 dpi; height defaults to width.

res

the resolution in dpi for the bitmap formats PNG and TIFF. Ignored for PDF and SVG.

create

logical; if TRUE, the files are written. Defaults to the option pharos.exportPlot, or FALSE if the option is not set.

screen

logical; if TRUE (default), the plot is also drawn on the current device when files are written. Without files (create = FALSE) the plot is always drawn on the current device.

Value

the paths of the written files as a character vector, invisibly; character(0) if create = FALSE.

Details

exportPlot() does not receive a finished plot but the plot call. The native pipe rewrites f(x) |> exportPlot() into exportPlot(f(x)), and since R evaluates arguments lazily, f(x) has not been run when exportPlot() starts. The call is captured with substitute() and evaluated once per output file on a freshly opened device, and finally once on the current device. Every file is therefore drawn at its own size and resolution: margins, label widths and font sizes that a plot function computes from the device (e.g. via strwidth()) are right for each format. Replaying a recorded plot (recordPlot()) would freeze the values computed on the screen device instead.

This only works with the native pipe |> or with a direct call exportPlot(plot(...), ...), which also accepts a braced block of several drawing calls (see Examples). The magrittr pipe %>% hands over a placeholder, not the call.

Repeated evaluation. Everything in expr runs once per output file and once more on the screen if requested (screen): assignments, messages, file operations and expensive computations included. Prepare the data beforehand and pass only the drawing calls.

Random numbers. If a random number generator state exists, it is restored before each evaluation, so every output starts from the same state, and the state after the call is that of a single evaluation. A plot that draws random numbers (jitter, sampling) then comes out the same in every file, as long as it consumes the same random numbers on every device; a plot that branches on device properties may not. In a fresh session in which no random number has been drawn yet there is no state to restore, and the outputs are not synchronised; call set.seed() first.

Graphics systems. Base graphics are drawn by the call itself. ggplot and trellis objects, which are only drawn when printed, are printed on each device; a grob is drawn on a new page with grid::grid.draw(). This applies only to a visible result, as at the console: exportPlot(p, ...) draws the ggplot p, while exportPlot(print(p), ...) draws it once through print(), which returns it invisibly. An object returned invisibly is never drawn automatically.

Switch. create defaults to the option pharos.exportPlot, which is FALSE unless set. A script thus decides in one place whether its figures are written, while single calls can still override it.

Devices. Each file device is closed by its own number after drawing, also if the plot call fails or opens or activates another device. The device that was current before the call is made current again, provided it is still open. If a file device cannot be opened, exportPlot() stops before drawing, with the device's own message as the reason; the current device is left untouched, and files of earlier types in type remain written.

See also

stamp() for the corner stamp, which plot functions in pharos draw by default and which is usually suppressed (stamp = FALSE) in figures for publication.

Examples

# without the switch, the plot is only drawn
plot(1:10) |>
  exportPlot(file.path(tempdir(), "demo"))


# write a PNG and a PDF, nothing on the screen
f <- plot(1:10, main = "Demo") |>
  exportPlot(file.path(tempdir(), "demo"), type = c("png", "pdf"),
             width = 4, create = TRUE, screen = FALSE)
f
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp4kvcRO/demo.png" "/tmp/Rtmp4kvcRO/demo.pdf"
file.exists(f)
#> [1] TRUE TRUE
unlink(f)

# a composed base plot: the model is fitted outside, as expr is
# evaluated once per file
fit <- lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
f <- exportPlot({
  plot(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
  abline(fit)
  legend("topleft", legend = "Regression", lty = 1)
}, file.path(tempdir(), "figure1"), create = TRUE, screen = FALSE)
unlink(f)

# switch it on for the whole script
opt <- options(pharos.exportPlot = TRUE)
f <- plot(1:10) |>
  exportPlot(file.path(tempdir(), "demo"), screen = FALSE)
unlink(f)
options(opt)
